subject: MeridianLite elevated error rate — routing fallback & recovery plan
body:
From: Sarah Price <sarah.price@cloudapps.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: support@cloudapps.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:12:14 -0700
Subject: spikes in MeridianLite errors impacting production

Hi Naomi / Ben,

We started seeing a significant uptick in generation failures and timeouts from the meridian-lite model around 08:45 PDT this morning. Approximately 7% of requests are returning 5xx / timeout errors (mostly 504s). This is across multiple endpoints in our service; latency is also climbing for long-context requests.

We've attached a snippet of the error log and a short request sample. Our platform can't silently degrade these paths — several customers are getting degraded experiences. Can you confirm whether this is a model-side issue or something on our routing? Any ETA for mitigation would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Sarah
Senior Product Manager | CloudApps Inc.

Hi Sarah — thanks for the report and the logs. We're seeing the same spike in telemetry from our side for the meridian-lite family (hosted).

Quick summary of what we're doing:
- Triage: eng oncall is investigating kernel/quantization paths and the serving runtime selection (started 09:25 PDT).
- Immediate mitigation: we've opened a routing policy to route your traffic to the meridian-small (compatible variant) as a fallback for any request that hits the 5xx threshold — this will be enabled in the next 10 minutes unless you opt out.
- Ops ticket: RD-12456 (tracking).

We expect the fallback to reduce error impact within the next 15 minutes; there may be brief session-level differences in responses. I'll update you when we have a root cause.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with a post-incident note and a recovery timeline.

— Naomi

Subject: MeridianLite elevated errors — root cause & closure

Hi Sarah — follow-up and closure. Thank you again for the prompt report and for tolerating the fallback period. Below is a concise summary and next steps; I'm attaching the diagnostic timeline and the minimal patch we applied.

Root cause (summary):
- At 08:30 PDT on Oct 25 we rolled a minor scheduler/kernelselection optimization to the hosted runtime aimed at improving throughput for quantized Meridian variants.
- A regression in the kernel-selection heuristics caused an incompatible quantized attention kernel to be chosen for a small subset of sequence-length/kv-cache states for meridian-lite. That combination produced increased memory pressure and led to recurrent 504s under specific request shapes.

Mitigation and recovery actions taken: 
- 09:40 PDT Oct 25: automatic fallback routing to meridian-small for CloudApps traffic (reduced customer errors to <0.5% within 20m).
- 11:15 PDT Oct 25: rolled back the scheduler heuristic to the prior stable commit (rollback RD-12456-RB1).
- 12:30–15:00 PDT Oct 25: progressive canary of corrected kernel-selection logic across shard groups; monitors green.
- 16:10 PDT Oct 25: full rollout of fix completed; error rates returned to baseline. We validated across your observed request shapes.

Impact and customer-facing commitments: 
- Total customer-visible error window: ~08:45–12:30 PDT (peak between 08:45–10:15).
- We will apply a goodwill credit to CloudApps for the incident period (details in separate billing note).
- Postmortem doc: link above; detailed timeline and remediation plan are in the Drive folder.

Follow-up work and prevention:
- Strengthened unit tests for kernel-selection permutations (PR RW-9872).
- New metric gating for sudden selection changes in canary windows.
- Expanded synthetic traffic shapes to include the request patterns you provided.

Attachments: initial-diagnostics.pdf, meridian-config-diff.patch (applied rollback patch).

If you'd like a short call to walk through the timeline and the patch, Ben and I are available tomorrow morning. Thanks again for the quick escalation.

Best,
